issues.legal_issue: A tenant inducted by a mortgagee in possession does not retain a right to remain in the property or claim rent-control protection against the mortgagor after redemption when the lease was not made in the course of prudent management.
material_facts: The owner mortgaged a shop and gave possession to the mortgagees, who were entitled to collect rent toward interest on the mortgage amount.
During the mortgage, the mortgagees let the shop to a tenant.
The mortgage was redeemed, and the decree ordered the mortgagees to deliver vacant possession to the owner.
The tenant was joined in the redemption suit and argued that the tenancy continued under the rent-control statute.
The finding that the letting was not an act of prudent management was not challenged and had become final.
issues.conclusion: The lease ended on redemption, the tenant could not claim rent-control protection against the mortgagor, and the mortgagor was entitled to recover possession.
issues.legal_principle: A mortgagee cannot confer an interest that continues beyond the mortgagee’s own interest. Under Section 76(a) and (e) of the Transfer of Property Act, 1882, a lease made in prudent management may bind the mortgagor, but a lease that does not qualify under that exception ends on redemption. When the mortgagee’s interest ends, the landlord-tenant relationship created by the mortgagee does not survive, so the tenant cannot claim protection under the rent-control statute against the mortgagor. The Court relied on Mahabir Gope v. Harbans Narain Singh, Harihar Prasad Singh v. Must. Of Munshi Nath Prasad, Asa Ram v. Mst. Ram Kali, All India Film Corp. Ltd. v. Sri Raja Gyan Nath, M/s Sachalmal Parasram v. Mst. Ratanbai, and Om Prakash Garg v. Ganga Sahai.

predicates.mortgage_redemption_proceeding: The proceeding sought redemption of a mortgage and recovery of the property for the owner.
predicates.mortgagee_created_lease: The mortgagee in possession let the property to a tenant during the mortgage.
predicates.mortgage_redeemed: The mortgage was redeemed, ending the mortgagee’s interest in the property.
predicates.lease_not_prudent_management: The lease was not made as an act of prudent management in the ordinary course.

issues.definition: When a lease made by a mortgagee during a mortgage is found not to be prudent management, redemption means the tenant has no right to remain after the mortgage ends.

issues.legal_issue: A lease made by a mortgagee in possession binds the mortgagor after redemption only if it was made in the course of prudent management.
material_facts: The mortgagees in possession let the mortgaged shop to a tenant during the mortgage.
The courts below found that the letting was not a prudent act in the ordinary course of management.
That finding was not challenged and became final.
issues.conclusion: The letting was not an act of prudent management and did not bind the mortgagor after redemption.
issues.legal_principle: Section 76(a) of the Transfer of Property Act, 1882, requires a mortgagee in possession to manage the property as a person of ordinary prudence would manage their own property. A lease that meets that standard may bind the mortgagor after redemption, but the person claiming the benefit of this exception must strictly establish it. The Court relied on Mahabir Gope v. Harbans Narain Singh, Harihar Prasad Singh v. Must. Of Munshi Nath Prasad, and Asa Ram v. Mst. Ram Kali.
